title: Type-Safe Builders and DSLs
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of type-safe builders and dsls using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates type-safe builders and dsls.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Type-Safe Builders and DSLs** as part of **Advanced Kotlin Language Features**. Apply type-safe builders and dsls by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Lambda Receivers, Building a Small Domain-Specific Language, Scope Control and DSL Readability—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Apply type-safe builders and dsls by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with lambda receivers. Then compare it with building a small domain-specific language. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Lambda Receivers
items.text: Lambda Receivers describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Building a Small Domain-Specific Language
items.text: Building a Small Domain-Specific Language should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Scope Control and DSL Readability
items.text: Scope Control and DSL Readability is one part of type-safe builders and dsls. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Compile with an explicitly selected Kotlin version and compiler options; experimental syntax is labelled and should be isolated from stable production code.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Type-Safe Builders and DSLs removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Describe the main rule of type-safe builders and dsls in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates type-safe builders and dsls. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving lambda receivers.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain type-safe builders and dsls without copying the lesson wording.
